title: The Hero With a Thousand Faces

questions.q: What are the three essential stages of the hero's journey?
a: The call, the quest, and the return
The departure, the trial, and the reward
The beginning, the middle, and the end
The problem, the solution, and the lesson
questions.why: The stages lesson lists the call, the quest, and the return as the three essential stages.

questions.q: What does the text say happens if the hero ignores his call?
a: He will feel unhappiness and misery
He will be punished by the gods
He will lose all his friends
He will become a villain in the story
questions.why: The stages lesson states that not answering your call will haunt your mind and cause misery.

questions.q: What does the text say about the hero's experience during the quest?
a: He must proceed feeling blind with no map to guide him
He is given a detailed map by a mentor
He can always return home if things get too hard
He is guaranteed success if he is brave enough
questions.why: The veil lesson says the hero must go through his quest feeling blind with no clue about what comes next.

questions.q: According to the text, what helped the hero fulfill his mission?
a: Consistency and determination, not extraordinary talent
A super power or outstanding circumstances
The help of a wise mentor throughout
A single moment of extraordinary courage
questions.why: The hard work lesson states it was not extraordinary talent but going little by little with determination.

questions.q: What term does Campbell use for the universal story pattern?
a: The Monomyth
The Archetype
The Paradigm
The Blueprint
questions.why: The overview states Campbell calls the universal arc of character development the Monomyth.
